documents.title: Demo: preparing a home for hurricane winds
documents.publisher: IslandReady AI (demonstration content — NOT official government guidance)
documents.text: IslandReady AI demonstration content — NOT official government guidance. Before hurricane season, close and test storm shutters on all windows and doors. Bring loose outdoor items such as chairs, bins, and sheets of zinc inside, or tie them down. Clear roof gutters, yard drains, and roadside channels so heavy rain can run off instead of pooling around the home.

documents.title: Demo: storing drinking water
documents.publisher: IslandReady AI (demonstration content — NOT official government guidance)
documents.text: IslandReady AI demonstration content — NOT official government guidance. Store one gallon of drinking water per person per day for at least three days. Keep water in clean, sealed containers in a cool place. Rotate stored water every six months and include extra water for babies and anyone with medical needs.

documents.title: Demo: storing emergency food including baby food
documents.publisher: IslandReady AI (demonstration content — NOT official government guidance)
documents.text: IslandReady AI demonstration content — NOT official government guidance. Keep a three-day supply of canned and dry food that needs no refrigeration or cooking. Add baby food and formula where needed, plus a manual can opener. Check expiry dates twice a year and replace anything past its date.

documents.title: Demo: radio, phone tree, and out-of-island contact
documents.publisher: IslandReady AI (demonstration content — NOT official government guidance)
documents.text: IslandReady AI demonstration content — NOT official government guidance. Keep a battery or wind-up radio with spare batteries and test it monthly. Agree a family phone tree and one out-of-island contact everyone checks in with, since local networks may fail while overseas calls still connect. Charge all phones and power banks before a storm.

documents.title: Demo: general shelter-packing list
documents.publisher: IslandReady AI (demonstration content — NOT official government guidance)
documents.text: IslandReady AI demonstration content — NOT official government guidance. A general shelter bag holds identification documents, medications, baby supplies, drinking water, a torch, and a radio. Confirm which shelter to use and how to get there through official channels at the time — this list does not name any specific shelter and says nothing about which shelters are open.

documents.title: Demo: hypothetical right-now response pattern (NOT a live event)
documents.publisher: IslandReady AI (demonstration content — NOT official government guidance)
documents.text: IslandReady AI demonstration content — NOT official government guidance. This describes a HYPOTHETICAL pattern only, not any actual emergency: if a household learned a storm might arrive in three days, a general pattern would be to check official alerts first, charge all devices, secure loose outdoor items, and confirm the family meeting point. Always follow real official instructions in a real event.

documents.title: Demo: drains, gutters, and flood preparation
documents.publisher: IslandReady AI (demonstration content — NOT official government guidance)
documents.text: IslandReady AI demonstration content — NOT official government guidance. Clear household drains, gutters, and nearby waterways before heavy rain so water drains away from the home. Move valuables, documents, and electrical items above likely flood level. Never walk or drive through floodwater.

documents.title: Demo: general steps after a storm passes
documents.publisher: IslandReady AI (demonstration content — NOT official government guidance)
documents.text: IslandReady AI demonstration content — NOT official government guidance. After a storm passes and officials say it is safe, check on relatives and neighbours, photograph any damage for assistance records, clear debris carefully, report damaged utilities to the authorities, and seek official guidance on water safety and relief assistance.
